title: O.4 Selection against collapse, and when a collapse path has a finite value
text:
Proof of (iii)

Proof. Step 8: where (R) holds, the aftermath is feasible and has a finite value. Let \(\gamma_C\equiv\left[\left(1-\delta\right)/\left(1+\rho\right)\right]^{1/\eta}\) and \(s^{\mathrm{stop}}\equiv\left(1-\delta\right)-\gamma_C\). Each of \(s^{\mathrm{stop}}>0\) and \(\beta\gamma_C^{1-\eta}<1\) is (R), since \(\gamma_C^\eta=\beta\left(1-\delta\right)\) gives \[
\gamma_C<1-\delta\iff\beta\left(1-\delta\right)^{1-\eta}<1,
\qquad
\beta\gamma_C^{1-\eta}=\Big[\beta\left(1-\delta\right)^{1-\eta}\Big]^{1/\eta},
\] and \(\beta\left(1-\delta\right)^{1-\eta}<1\) is (R). Let (R) hold, and let the stocks at a date \(\tau\ge0\) be the initial ones if \(\tau=0\), and otherwise those of a path feasible through \(\tau-1\), with \(K_\tau>0\). From \(\tau\) on, set \(N_t=D_t=0\), \(\varpi_t=0\), \(K^R_t=0\), \(\Omega_t=0\), \(C_t=s^{\mathrm{stop}}K_t\) and \(K_{t+1}=\gamma_CK_t\), and let the states follow the transitions.
This is feasible. With no treated flow nothing is recovered, so \(R_t=0<\bar R\) and \(Y_t=0\). Every cost flow is zero: \(C^N\left(0,S,t\right)=C^D\left(0,X,t\right)=0\), and \(C^W_t=c^T\left(0\right)H_t=0\). The goods constraint reads \(C_t+I_t+\delta K_t=\left[s^{\mathrm{stop}}+\gamma_C-\left(1-\delta\right)\right]K_t=0=Y_t\). The intensity condition holds as \(0=0\). With \(\Omega_t=0\), \(M^K_{t+1}=\left(1-\delta\right)M^K_t\ge0\), and the ledger gives \(W_t=R_t-\Delta M^K_{t+1}=\delta M^K_t\ge0\). \(K_t=\gamma_C^{t-\tau}K_\tau>0\), so \(C_t>0\), \(K_{t+1}>0\) and \(K^R_t=0\le K_t\); the other controls are zero; and \(S\) and \(X\) keep their values at \(\tau\), so every domain and mass restriction of Problem 1 holds. No date from \(\tau\) on operates.
Its value from \(\tau\) on is finite. With \(j\equiv t-\tau\), \(C_t=s^{\mathrm{stop}}K_\tau\gamma_C^j\), so for \(\eta\ne1\) the sum \(\sum_{t\ge\tau}\beta^tu\left(C_t\right)\) is \(\beta^\tau\left(s^{\mathrm{stop}}K_\tau\right)^{1-\eta}/\left(1-\eta\right)\) times \(\sum_{j\ge0}\left[\beta\gamma_C^{1-\eta}\right]^j<\infty\), and at \(\eta=1\) it is \(\beta^\tau\sum_{j\ge0}\beta^j\left[\ln\left(s^{\mathrm{stop}}K_\tau\right)+j\ln\gamma_C\right]\), which converges absolutely. For pollution, \(\varpi_t=0\) and \(\mathcal N_t=0\) give \(\Xi_t=\mu\mathcal W_t\), and the transitions of \(M^K\) and \(\mathcal W\) add to \(\mathcal M_{t+1}=\mathcal M_t-\mu\mathcal W_t\), with \(\mathcal M_t\equiv M^K_t+\mathcal W_t\ge0\). So \(\sum_{t\ge\tau}\Xi_t\le\mathcal M_\tau\), and \(P_{t+1}\le P_t+\Xi_t\) gives \(0\le P_t\le P_\tau+\mathcal M_\tau\) for \(t\ge\tau\). As \(v\) is increasing, \(v\left(P_t\right)\) lies between \(v\left(0\right)\) and \(v\left(P_\tau+\mathcal M_\tau\right)\), and \(\sum_{t\ge\tau}\beta^tv\left(P_t\right)\) converges absolutely.
Step 9: (iii). Let \(K_0>0\) and let (R) hold. The aftermath from \(\tau=0\) never operates, so it is a collapse path, and its value is finite by step 8. If (R) fails, every collapse path has value \(-\infty\), by (i). So (R) holds exactly when some collapse path has a finite value.

title: O.5 Selection against balanced dematerialization
text:
The statements
Proposition 8 of the paper (selection against balanced dematerialization) states that in the floorless Cobb-Douglas workhorse a path in state B is beaten by a late switch to full treatment, so that no optimal path with a finite value ends in state B. This page proves it in full and adds a corollary of its own, the growth gap, which compares the growth of a state-B path of the workhorse, at the rates of the paper’s Appendix B.6, with that of the closed loop. Symbols are the paper’s, as on the notation page; a symbol the proof needs beyond them is defined where it is first used.
Proposition 8 (selection against balanced dematerialization). Take the Cobb-Douglas workhorse without a floor, under the soft ceiling with a stationary yield function, CRRA utility and \(\phi^I=0\). Every state-B path with \(\beta\left(1+g\right)^{1-\eta}<1\) has a finite value and is strictly improved on by a path that copies it until a late date and then treats all handled waste, with enough added recycling capital that less of the waste stock is lost each period, provided either (a) \(\left(1-\nu\right)\left(1+g\right)^{\eta-1}<1\), for any yield with the soft ceiling, or (b) \(g>0\) and the yield tail is at least as thin as exponential. With the exponential yield, (a) or (b) holds for every state-B path with \(\beta\left(1+g\right)^{1-\eta}<1\), so no optimal path with a finite value is in state B, except at the knife-edge \(\beta\left(1+g\right)^{1-\eta}=1\).
The growth gap (a corollary of the workhorse’s rates, Appendix B.6). Every state-B path of the workhorse grows more slowly than the closed loop and faster than its matter decays, \(1-\nu<1+g<1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}\). For a candidate with converging recycling margins the production function and the extraction margin fix the rates jointly (Appendix B.6), and its growth rate \(g^{\mathrm{dem}}\) satisfies \[
1+g^{\mathrm{dem}}=\left(1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}\right)^{\frac{\left(\mu_N-1\right)\left(1-\beta_K\right)}{\left(\mu_N-1\right)\left(1-\beta_K\right)+\gamma}}\;<\;1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}
\qquad\text{for }\left(\mu_N-1\right)\left(1-\beta_K\right)+\gamma>0 .
\]
In the growth gap, \(\mu_N\) is the elasticity with which the workhorse’s marginal extraction cost rises as the reserve falls (Section 3).
Three cases are not covered by the proposition: tails slower than exponential where \(\eta>1\), \(g>0\) and (a) fails, some power tails among them; material input decaying more slowly than any geometric rate, or \(R\) decaying at a rate other than that of \(\mathcal W\); and \(\phi^I>0\), where the switch changes the storage share.
We take the simplest route for the paper’s assumptions. The proposition compares feasible paths, and we prove it by building the switch and bounding the difference in value, with no first-order condition. The Cobb-Douglas form enters the comparison of output across the two paths and the growth gap; the thin tail enters case (b) only; and one property of pollution decay, that it does not tip near zero, enters case (a) only.

title: O.5 Selection against balanced dematerialization
text:
What the proof uses
From the shared page. The shared lemmas for the long-run proofs restate the paper’s model as these proofs use it. We use the definition of a feasible path given there: the constraints and domains of Problem 1, the three restrictions on masses \(S_t\ge0\), \(X_t\le\bar X_{\max}\) and \(M^K_t\ge0\), nonnegative initial stocks, \(K^R_t\le K_t\), and gross capital formation free in sign. We use the nonnegativity of every cost flow, the material budget \(\mathcal B\equiv\bar N+M^K_0+\mathcal W_0\) with \(\bar N\equiv S_0+\bar X_{\max}-X_0\), and Lemma A: (a) \(\sum_tN_t\le\bar N\) and \(\sum_tD_t\le\bar X_{\max}-X_0\), so \(N_t\to0\), and \(D_t\to0\) likewise; (b) \(\mathcal W_t\le\mathcal B\) at every date and \(\sum_t\left(1-a_t\varpi_t\right)H_t\le\mathcal B\). The proof of Lemma A uses only the material constraints: the ledger, \(R=N+a\varpi H\), the transitions of \(S\), \(X\), \(M^K\) and \(\mathcal W\), the domains \(N,D,K^R,W\ge0\) and \(\varpi\in\left[0,1\right]\), the restrictions on masses and nonnegative initial stocks. We call a path that meets these and the pollution transition materially feasible; Lemma A holds on it.
From the paper’s model (Section 2). The flow reaching the environment is \(\Xi=\Xi^h+\mathcal N\), with \(\Xi^h\equiv\left[1-\varpi+d^W\varpi\left(1-a\right)\right]H\) the emission of the handled stream, \(0<d^W<1\), and \(\mathcal N=\Omega^{N,S}N+\Omega^{D,S}D\) the displaced mass, \(\Omega^{N,S},\Omega^{D,S}\ge0\). Both handling charges are non-increasing in time, so the handling cost per handled tonne at full treatment satisfies \(c^c\left(t\right)+c^T\left(1,t\right)\le c^{\mathrm{full}}\equiv c^c\left(0\right)+c^T\left(1,0\right)\), finite because \(c^T\) is convex with \(c^T\left(0\right)=0\) and \(c^{T\prime}\left(1\right)<\infty\). We read the relative intensities as nonnegative, \(\omega^j\ge0\), each use releasing waste. We write \(\mathcal P\left(P\right)\equiv\left[1-\theta\left(P\right)\right]P\), so the pollution transition is \(P_{t+1}=\mathcal P\left(P_t\right)+\Xi_t\).
From the paper’s long-run section (Section 3).

Rates: “A variable \(Z\) grows at rate \(g\) when \(Z_{t+1}/Z_t\to1+g\) and decays at rate \(\nu\in\left(0,1\right)\) when \(Z_{t+1}/Z_t\to1-\nu\)”; the gross factor is positive, \(1+g>0\) (the notation page, rule 8).
State B (Definition 1): “balanced dematerialization if \(C_t>0\) at every date and, asymptotically, \(C\), \(Y\) and \(K^Y\) grow at a common rate \(g\) with \(Y/C\) bounded above and away from zero, while \(R\) and \(\mathcal W\) decay at a common rate \(\nu\in\left(0,1\right)\)”. We call \(\left(g,\nu\right)\) the path’s rates. The ratios of consecutive terms being defined, \(Y\), \(K^Y\), \(R\) and \(\mathcal W\) are positive from some date on, and there are constants \(0<\underline o\le\bar o\) with \(\underline o\le Y_t/C_t\le\bar o\) from some date on.
The workhorse: output “\(A_te^{-\kappa P}\left(K^Y\right)^{\beta_K}\left(B_tR^e\right)^{\gamma}\) with \(\beta_K+\gamma<1\)”, where \(\beta_K,\gamma>0\) and \(\kappa\ge0\), and without a floor \(R^e=R\); the trends of Assumption 1(i), “\(A_{t+1}/A_t=1+g_A\), \(B_{t+1}/B_t=1+g_B\), \(g_A,g_B\ge0\) and \(g_A+g_B>0\)”, with “\(\Gamma\equiv\left(1+g_A\right)\left(1+g_B\right)^{\gamma}>1\)”; the circular rate \(g^{\mathrm{circ}}\) of “\(\left(1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}\right)^{1-\beta_K}=\Gamma\)”; “the exponential yield \(a\left(x\right)=\bar a\left(1-e^{-\xi x}\right)\)”, under the soft ceiling \(1-e^{-\xi x}\); and “CRRA utility”, \(u\left(C\right)=C^{1-\eta}/\left(1-\eta\right)\) with \(\eta>0\), and \(\ln C\) at \(\eta=1\). The workhorse’s extraction cost enters only through \(\mu_N\), in the growth gap.
A stationary yield function under the soft ceiling, which the proposition puts in place of the exponential yield: a function \(a\left(x\right)\) of the intensity alone with the properties of Section 2 at \(\bar a=1\), \(a\left(0\right)=0\), \(a'>0\), \(a''<0\) and \(a\left(x\right)\to1\). It is continuous and strictly increasing with \(a<1\), so its inverse \(a^{-1}:\left[0,1\right)\to\left[0,\infty\right)\) is defined.
Assumption 1(iii), from the paper’s statement of what it assumes about the long run: “Regeneration. \(\theta\left(P\right)\ge\theta_{\min}>0\) for all \(P\), and \(\rho+\theta\left(P\right)+\theta'\left(P\right)P>0\) on the relevant range.” The paper’s Appendix A says of the pollution price that where \(r+\theta+\theta'P\le0\) “the forward sum need not converge, this model’s tipping point, ruled out by a restriction on \(\theta\) named in Section 3”; that restriction is this second clause. It is the second route to the property case (a) uses near zero, and nothing else on this page uses it.

Readings of the statement.

The loss rate of the waste stock is \(\ell_t\equiv\mu\left(1-a_t\varpi_t\right)\in\left[0,\mu\right]\), so that \(\ell_t\mathcal W_t=\left(1-a_t\varpi_t\right)H_t\) is the leakage flow and \(\left(\mu-\ell_t\right)\mathcal W_t=a_t\varpi_tH_t\) the recovered flow; at a date with no treated flow \(a_t\varpi_t\equiv0\), as on the shared page. “Less of the waste stock is lost each period” is a lower loss rate.
The yield tail is at least as thin as exponential, a thin tail for short, when there are \(\xi>0\) and \(c_\xi\ge1\) with \(1-a\left(x\right)\le c_\xi e^{-\xi x}\) for all \(x\ge0\); the exponential yield has a thin tail with \(c_\xi=1\).
The value of a path is \(U_0=\lim_{T\to\infty}\sum_{t=0}^{T}\beta^t\left[u\left(C_t\right)-v\left(P_t\right)\right]\) where the limit exists in \(\left[-\infty,+\infty\right]\), and an optimal path is a feasible path whose value is the supremum of values over feasible paths.
Pollution does not tip near zero when there is \(P_+>0\) with \(\rho+\theta\left(P\right)+\theta'\left(P\right)P>0\) for all \(P\in\left[0,P_+\right]\). The paper’s model has this property, since it takes \(\theta\) continuously differentiable (Section 2, as the shared page restates): \(\theta'\) is then bounded near zero, so \(\theta'\left(P\right)P\to0\) as \(P\to0\), while \(\rho+\theta\left(0\right)>0\). Assumption 1(iii) gives it a second way, since pollution tends to zero on every state-B path (Lemma Z, in A path in state B), so the levels near zero are in the relevant range.

section: Pollution on a materially feasible path
text:
Pollution on a materially feasible path
Lemma E. On every materially feasible path:
(a) \(0\le P_t\le\bar P\equiv P_0+\mathcal B+\Omega^{N,S}\bar N+\Omega^{D,S}\left(\bar X_{\max}-X_0\right)\) at every date;
(b) \(\mathcal P\) is strictly increasing on \(\left[0,\infty\right)\);
(c) for all dates \(t\ge s\), \(P_t\le\left[1-\theta\left(\bar P\right)\right]^{t-s}P_s+\bar\Xi_s/\theta\left(\bar P\right)\), with \(\bar\Xi_s\equiv\sup_{r\ge s}\Xi_r\); so \(P_t\to0\) when \(\Xi_t\to0\).

Proof. 

\(\mathcal P'\left(P\right)=1-\theta\left(P\right)-\theta'\left(P\right)P>0\), since \(\theta<1\), \(\theta'<0\) and \(P\ge0\).
Every term of \(\Xi\) is nonnegative: the bracket of \(\Xi^h\) because \(\varpi\in\left[0,1\right]\) and \(a\le1\), and \(\mathcal N\) because \(N,D\ge0\). From \(P_0\ge0\) and \(\theta\in\left(0,1\right)\), \(P_{t+1}=\mathcal P\left(P_t\right)+\Xi_t\) lies in \(\left[0,P_t+\Xi_t\right]\), so \(P_t\ge0\) and \(P_t\le P_0+\sum_{s<t}\Xi_s\). Since \(d^W<1\), \(\Xi^h_s\le\left[\left(1-\varpi_s\right)+\varpi_s\left(1-a_s\right)\right]H_s=\left(1-a_s\varpi_s\right)H_s\), whose sum is at most \(\mathcal B\) by Lemma A(b), and \(\sum_s\mathcal N_s\le\Omega^{N,S}\bar N+\Omega^{D,S}\left(\bar X_{\max}-X_0\right)\) by Lemma A(a).
By (a) and \(\theta'<0\), \(\theta\left(P_t\right)\ge\theta\left(\bar P\right)>0\), so \(P_{t+1}\le\left[1-\theta\left(\bar P\right)\right]P_t+\Xi_t\). The bound holds at \(t=s\), and if it holds at \(t\), then \(P_{t+1}\le\left[1-\theta\left(\bar P\right)\right]^{t+1-s}P_s+\left[1-\theta\left(\bar P\right)\right]\bar\Xi_s/\theta\left(\bar P\right)+\bar\Xi_s\), which is the bound at \(t+1\). If \(\Xi_t\to0\), choose \(s\) with \(\bar\Xi_s\) small and then \(t\) large.

title: O.5 Selection against balanced dematerialization
text:
A path in state B
Lemma Z. Let \(z\) be a feasible path in state B with rates \(\left(g,\nu\right)\), in the Cobb-Douglas workhorse without a floor and with CRRA utility, under any yield function and any \(\phi^I\ge0\).
(a) \(P_t\to0\), and \(\left(1+g\right)^{1-\beta_K}=\Gamma\left(1-\nu\right)^{\gamma}\); hence \(1-\nu<1+g<1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}\).
(b) \(\mathcal W_t/C_t\to0\); and if \(\left(1-\nu\right)\left(1+g\right)^{\eta-1}<1\), then \(\left(1+t\right)\mathcal W_tC_t^{\eta-1}\to0\).
(c) If \(\Pi\equiv\beta\left(1+g\right)^{1-\eta}<1\), the value of \(z\) is finite, and for every \(\upsilon\in\left(0,\min\left\{\Pi,1-\Pi\right\}\right)\) there is a date \(T_\upsilon\) such that \(\pi_t\equiv\beta^tC_t^{1-\eta}\) satisfies \[
\pi_s\left(\Pi-\upsilon\right)^{t-s}\;\le\;\pi_t\;\le\;\pi_s\left(\Pi+\upsilon\right)^{t-s}\qquad\text{for }t\ge s\ge T_\upsilon .
\]
(d) If \(\phi^I=0\), then at every date, with the inflow \(n_t\equiv N_t+\delta M^K_t\ge0\),  \[
\mathcal W_{t+1}=\left(1-\ell_t\right)\mathcal W_t+n_t,
\qquad
R_t=N_t+\left(\mu-\ell_t\right)\mathcal W_t\;\le\;\mathcal W_{t+1};
\tag{W}
\] and for every \(\upsilon\in\left(0,\min\left\{\nu,1-\nu\right\}\right)\) there is a date \(T'_\upsilon\) such that, for \(t\ge s\ge T'_\upsilon\), \[
\left(1-\nu-\upsilon\right)^{t-s}\mathcal W_s\le\mathcal W_t\le\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)^{t-s}\mathcal W_s,
\qquad
\ell_t\ge\nu-\upsilon,
\qquad
n_t\le\ell_t\mathcal W_t\le\mu\mathcal W_t,
\qquad
\sum_{r\ge s}\mathcal W_r\le\frac{\mathcal W_s}{\nu-\upsilon} .
\] In particular \(\nu\le\mu\).

Proof. 

\(\Xi^h_t\le H_t=\mu\mathcal W_t\to0\), the bracket being at most one, and \(\mathcal N_t\to0\) by Lemma A(a); so \(\Xi_t\to0\), and Lemma E(c) gives \(P_t\to0\). Output is positive from some date on, and \(A_t\), \(B_t\) follow the trends, so \[
\frac{Y_{t+1}}{Y_t}=\left(1+g_A\right)\left(1+g_B\right)^{\gamma}e^{-\kappa\left(P_{t+1}-P_t\right)}\left(\frac{K^Y_{t+1}}{K^Y_t}\right)^{\beta_K}\left(\frac{R_{t+1}}{R_t}\right)^{\gamma}\;\longrightarrow\;\Gamma\left(1+g\right)^{\beta_K}\left(1-\nu\right)^{\gamma},
\] while the left side tends to \(1+g>0\); dividing by \(\left(1+g\right)^{\beta_K}\) gives the identity. Since \(\left(1-\nu\right)^{\gamma}<1\), \(\left(1+g\right)^{1-\beta_K}<\Gamma=\left(1+g^{\mathrm{circ}}\right)^{1-\beta_K}\). Since \(\Gamma>1\), \(0<1-\nu<1\) and \(\gamma<1-\beta_K\), \(\left(1+g\right)^{1-\beta_K}>\left(1-\nu\right)^{\gamma}>\left(1-\nu\right)^{1-\beta_K}\).
The ratio of consecutive terms of \(\mathcal W_t/C_t\) tends to \(\left(1-\nu\right)/\left(1+g\right)\), below one by (a), and that of \(\left(1+t\right)\mathcal W_tC_t^{\eta-1}\) to \(\left(1-\nu\right)\left(1+g\right)^{\eta-1}\). A positive sequence whose ratio tends to a limit below one tends to zero.
\(\pi_{t+1}/\pi_t=\beta\left(C_{t+1}/C_t\right)^{1-\eta}\to\Pi\), so the ratio lies in \(\left[\Pi-\upsilon,\Pi+\upsilon\right]\) from some date \(T_\upsilon\) on, and iterating gives the bounds. For \(\eta\ne1\), \(\sum_t\beta^t\left|u\left(C_t\right)\right|=\sum_t\pi_t/\left|1-\eta\right|<\infty\) by the upper bound, as \(\Pi+\upsilon<1\). For \(\eta=1\), \(\left|\ln C_t\right|\le\left|\ln C_0\right|+bt\) with \(b\equiv\sup_s\left|\ln\left(C_{s+1}/C_s\right)\right|\), finite because the sequence converges and \(C_s>0\) at every date, so \(\sum_t\beta^t\left|\ln C_t\right|<\infty\). By Lemma E(a) pollution stays in \(\left[0,\bar P\right]\), where the continuous \(v\) is bounded, so \(\sum_t\beta^tv\left(P_t\right)\) converges absolutely. The value is finite.
With \(\phi^I=0\), \(\Phi^I=0\), so \(M^K_t=\left(1-\delta\right)^tM^K_0\ge0\) and the ledger reads \(W_t=R_t+\delta M^K_t\). With \(R_t=N_t+a_t\varpi_t\mu\mathcal W_t=N_t+\left(\mu-\ell_t\right)\mathcal W_t\), the waste-stock transition gives (W), and \(R_t\le W_t\le\mathcal W_{t+1}\). Let \(T'_\upsilon\) be a date from which \(\mathcal W_t>0\) and \(\mathcal W_{t+1}/\mathcal W_t\) lies within \(\upsilon\) of \(1-\nu\); \(\mathcal W\) decreases from then on, as \(1-\nu+\upsilon<1\). Iterating the bounds on \(\mathcal W_{t+1}/\mathcal W_t\) gives the first display and the geometric sum. By (W), \(\ell_t\mathcal W_t=\mathcal W_t-\mathcal W_{t+1}+n_t\ge\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)\mathcal W_t\) and \(n_t=\ell_t\mathcal W_t-\left(\mathcal W_t-\mathcal W_{t+1}\right)\le\ell_t\mathcal W_t\), while \(\ell_t\le\mu\) since \(a_t\varpi_t\ge0\). Finally \(\nu-\upsilon\le\mu\) for every small \(\upsilon\) gives \(\nu\le\mu\).

title: O.5 Selection against balanced dematerialization
text:
Proof of Proposition 8
Let \(z\) be a state-B path with rates \(\left(g,\nu\right)\), \(\phi^I=0\) and \(\Pi\equiv\beta\left(1+g\right)^{1-\eta}<1\). Its value is finite by Lemma Z(c). We build the switch \(z'\), with primes for its variables, and show that its value exceeds that of \(z\) for every late enough switch date.

Proof. Step 1: the constants and the common part of the switch. Fix \[
0<\upsilon<\tfrac14\min\left\{\nu,\;\nu+g,\;1-\nu,\;\Pi,\;1-\Pi\right\},
\qquad\text{and in case (b) also }\upsilon<g/2 ,
\] where \(\nu+g>0\) by Lemma Z(a). Let \(T_0\) be a date from which the bounds of Lemma Z(c) and (d) hold with this \(\upsilon\), \(Y_t\), \(K^Y_t\) and \(R_t\) are positive, \(\underline o\le Y_t/C_t\le\bar o\), and \(\left(1+g-\upsilon\right)C_t\le C_{t+1}\le\left(1+g+\upsilon\right)C_t\). The switch date is any \(T_1\ge T_0+1\); further lower bounds on \(T_1\) are collected as they arise, and no constant below depends on \(T_1\).
The path \(z'\) has the controls of \(z\) through \(T_1-2\), and at \(T_1-1\) those of \(z\) except investment, consumption and the intensity \(\Omega\). From \(T_1\) on it extracts and explores as \(z\) does, \(N'_t=N_t\) and \(D'_t=D_t\). It treats all handled waste, \(\varpi'_t=1\), at an intensity \(x'_t\) set by the rule of step 2 or step 3, with recycling capital \(K^{R\prime}_t\equiv x'_t\mu\mathcal W'_t\). It finances that capital with the added capital \(Q_t\equiv\max\left\{0,K^{R\prime}_t-K^R_t\right\}\) held on top of the capital of \(z\), \(K'_t\equiv K_t+Q_t\), with \(Q_t\equiv0\) for \(t<T_1\), so that it invests \(I'_t=I_t+Q_{t+1}-Q_t\) from \(T_1-1\) on. Consumption \(C'_t\) is the goods constraint solved for it, \(W'_t\) is given by the ledger, \(\Omega'_t\equiv R'_t/\mathcal D'_t\), and the states follow the transitions. Four consequences follow.

Production capital never falls below that of \(z\): \(K^{Y\prime}_t=K'_t-K^{R\prime}_t=K^Y_t+\max\left\{0,K^R_t-K^{R\prime}_t\right\}\ge K^Y_t\) for \(t\ge T_1\).
With \(\phi^I=0\), neither the ledger nor any transition of a material stock or of pollution involves \(C\), \(I\) or \(\Omega\), so period \(T_1-1\) has the material block of \(z\): \(\mathcal W'_{T_1}=\mathcal W_{T_1}\) and \(P'_{T_1}=P_{T_1}\). \(S'\), \(X'\) and \(M^{K\prime}\) equal \(S\), \(X\) and \(M^K\) at every date, and so does the inflow \(n_t\) of (W).
For \(t\ge T_1\), with the loss rate \(\ell'_t=\mu\left[1-a\left(x'_t\right)\right]\), the argument of (W) gives \(R'_t=N_t+\left(\mu-\ell'_t\right)\mathcal W'_t\) and \(\mathcal W'_{t+1}=\left(1-\ell'_t\right)\mathcal W'_t+n_t\), and at \(\varpi'=1\) the flow reaching the environment is \(\Xi'_t=d^W\ell'_t\mathcal W'_t+\mathcal N_t\), with the displaced mass of \(z\). On \(z\), since \(d^W<1\), \(\Xi_t\ge d^W\left(1-a_t\varpi_t\right)H_t+\mathcal N_t=d^W\ell_t\mathcal W_t+\mathcal N_t\).
The stock gap \(w_t\equiv\mathcal W'_t-\mathcal W_t\) has \(w_{T_1}=0\) and, for \(t\ge T_1\),  \[
w_{t+1}=w_t-\ell'_t\mathcal W'_t+\ell_t\mathcal W_t,
\qquad
R'_t-R_t=\mu w_t-\ell'_t\mathcal W'_t+\ell_t\mathcal W_t .
\tag{W'}
\]

Once a rule fixes \(x'_t\), the switch is materially feasible: the ledger and the transitions hold by construction, \(N'_t,D'_t\ge0\), \(\varpi'_t=1\), \(K^{R\prime}_t\ge0\), \(W'_t=R'_t+\delta M^K_t\ge0\), and \(S'\), \(X'\) and \(M^{K\prime}\) are those of \(z\). So Lemmas A and E apply to it before its consumption is known to be positive.
Step 2: case (b), the half-leakage rule. Let \(g>0\) and the yield have a thin tail. The rule is \[
1-a\left(x'_t\right)=\frac{\ell_t\mathcal W_t}{2\mu\mathcal W'_t},
\qquad\text{that is}\qquad
\ell'_t\mathcal W'_t=\tfrac12\ell_t\mathcal W_t :
\] the switch loses half the tonnes \(z\) loses. For \(t\ge T_1\):

(b1) The rule is well defined and the stock gap grows. If \(w_t\ge0\), true at \(T_1\), the right side of the rule lies in \(\left(0,\frac12\right]\), since \(0<\nu-\upsilon\le\ell_t\le\mu\) and \(0<\mathcal W_t\le\mathcal W'_t\); so \(x'_t=a^{-1}\left(1-\ell_t\mathcal W_t/\left(2\mu\mathcal W'_t\right)\right)\) exists, \(a\left(x'_t\right)\ge\frac12\), and (W’) gives \(w_{t+1}=w_t+\frac12\ell_t\mathcal W_t\ge w_t\). By induction \(w_t=\frac12\sum_{r=T_1}^{t-1}\ell_r\mathcal W_r\ge0\), and the loss rate is lower, \(\ell'_t=\frac12\ell_t\mathcal W_t/\mathcal W'_t\le\frac12\ell_t\).
(b2) The stock is bounded. By Lemma Z(d), \(w_t\le\frac\mu2\sum_{r\ge T_1}\mathcal W_r\le\mu\mathcal W_{T_1}/\left[2\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)\right]\) and \(\mathcal W_t\le\mathcal W_{T_1}\), so \(\mathcal W'_t\le\bar w_b\mathcal W_{T_1}\) with \(\bar w_b\equiv1+\mu/\left[2\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)\right]\).
(b3) The intensity grows at most linearly. By Lemma Z(d) and (b2), \(1-a\left(x'_t\right)\ge\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)\mathcal W_t/\left(2\mu\bar w_b\mathcal W_{T_1}\right)\ge\frac{\nu-\upsilon}{2\mu\bar w_b}\left(1-\nu-\upsilon\right)^{t-T_1}\), and the thin tail gives \(x\le\xi^{-1}\ln\left[c_\xi/\left(1-a\left(x\right)\right)\right]\) at every \(x\), so \[
x'_t\;\le\;\frac{b_0+b_1\left(t-T_1\right)}{\xi},
\qquad
b_0\equiv\ln\frac{2\mu\bar w_bc_\xi}{\nu-\upsilon},
\qquad
b_1\equiv\ln\frac1{1-\nu-\upsilon} .
\]
(b4) More material at every date, and eventually much more. By (W’) and the rule, \(R'_t-R_t=\mu w_t+\frac12\ell_t\mathcal W_t\ge0\). For \(t\ge T_1+1\), (b1) gives \(R'_t\ge a\left(x'_t\right)\mu\mathcal W'_t\ge\frac\mu2w_t\ge\frac\mu4\ell_{T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1}\ge\frac\mu4\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)\mathcal W_{T_1}\), while \(R_t\le\mathcal W_{t+1}\le\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)^{t+1-T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1}\) by (W) and Lemma Z(d); so \[
\frac{R'_t}{R_t}\;\ge\;c_R\,\vartheta^{\,t-T_1}\quad\left(t\ge T_1+1\right),
\qquad
c_R\equiv\frac{\mu\left(\nu-\upsilon\right)}{4\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)},
\qquad
\vartheta\equiv\frac1{1-\nu+\upsilon}>1 .
\]
(b5) Less pollution at every date. By step 1 and the rule, \(\Xi'_t=\frac12d^W\ell_t\mathcal W_t+\mathcal N_t\le\Xi_t\). From \(P'_{T_1}=P_{T_1}\), Lemma E(b) gives by induction \(P'_{t+1}=\mathcal P\left(P'_t\right)+\Xi'_t\le\mathcal P\left(P_t\right)+\Xi_t=P_{t+1}\).

Step 3: case (a), the fixed-intensity rule. Let \(\left(1-\nu\right)\left(1+g\right)^{\eta-1}<1\), the yield be any stationary yield under the soft ceiling, and pollution not tip near zero, on \(\left[0,P_+\right]\). Put \(\nu'\equiv\frac12\left[\max\left\{0,-g\right\}+\nu\right]\). Since \(\nu-\max\left\{0,-g\right\}=\min\left\{\nu,\nu+g\right\}>4\upsilon\), \[
\max\left\{0,-g\right\}+2\upsilon\;<\;\nu'\;<\;\nu-2\upsilon,
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
0<\nu'<\nu\le\mu
\quad\text{and}\quad
1-\nu'<1+g-2\upsilon .
\] The rule is \(x'_t\equiv x^\circ\equiv a^{-1}\left(1-\nu'/\mu\right)\), defined because \(\nu'/\mu\in\left(0,1\right)\), so the loss rate is lower at every date, \(\ell'_t=\nu'<\nu-\upsilon\le\ell_t\). Write \(\vartheta\equiv\left(1-\nu'\right)/\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)>1\). For \(t\ge T_1\):

(a1) The stock gap is positive and decays no faster than at \(\nu'\). (W’) reads \(w_{t+1}=\left(1-\nu'\right)w_t+\left(\ell_t-\nu'\right)\mathcal W_t\), with \(\ell_t-\nu'>\upsilon\); so \(w_t\ge0\), \(w_{T_1+1}\ge\left(\nu-\upsilon-\nu'\right)\mathcal W_{T_1}\), and \(w_t\ge\left(1-\nu'\right)^{t-T_1-1}w_{T_1+1}\) for \(t\ge T_1+1\).
(a2) The stock decays at the rate \(\nu'\). Solving the recursion of \(\mathcal W'\), and bounding \(n_r\le\mu\mathcal W_r\le\mu\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)^{r-T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1}\) by Lemma Z(d), so that the sum is at most \(\mu\mathcal W_{T_1}\left(1-\nu'\right)^{t-1-T_1}\sum_{j\ge0}\vartheta^{-j}\), \[
\mathcal W'_t=\left(1-\nu'\right)^{t-T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1}+\sum_{r=T_1}^{t-1}\left(1-\nu'\right)^{t-1-r}n_r\;\le\;\bar w_a\left(1-\nu'\right)^{t-T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1},
\qquad
\bar w_a\equiv1+\frac{\mu}{\left(1-\nu'\right)\left(1-\vartheta^{-1}\right)} .
\]
(a3) More material at every date, and eventually much more. By (W’), \(R'_t-R_t=\left(\mu-\nu'\right)w_t+\left(\ell_t-\nu'\right)\mathcal W_t\ge0\). For \(t\ge T_1+1\), \(R'_t\ge\left(\mu-\nu'\right)w_t\) and \(R_t\le\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)^{t+1-T_1}\mathcal W_{T_1}\), so with (a1) \[
\frac{R'_t}{R_t}\;\ge\;c_R\,\vartheta^{\,t-T_1}\quad\left(t\ge T_1+1\right),
\qquad
c_R\equiv\frac{\left(\mu-\nu'\right)\left(\nu-\upsilon-\nu'\right)}{\left(1-\nu'\right)\left(1-\nu+\upsilon\right)} .
\]
(a4) Pollution stays close. Emissions are not ordered here: the switch holds a larger stock and eventually emits more. The displaced mass cancels from the difference, and both handled streams lie in \(\left[0,\mu\mathcal W'_t\right]\), so by (a2) \(\left|\Xi'_t-\Xi_t\right|\le\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}\). A uniform bound comes first. The switch is materially feasible by step 1, so Lemma E(c) from \(s=T_1\), applied to both paths with \(\Xi_r\le\mu\mathcal W_r+\mathcal N_r\) and \(\Xi'_r\le\mu\mathcal W'_r+\mathcal N_r\), gives \[
\bar P_{T_1}\equiv\sup_{t\ge T_1}\max\left\{P_t,P'_t\right\}\;\le\;P_{T_1}+\frac{\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}+\sup_{r\ge T_1}\mathcal N_r}{\theta\left(\bar P\right)},
\] which tends to zero as \(T_1\to\infty\), by Lemma Z(a), Lemma Z(d) and Lemma A(a). Take \(T_1\) large enough that \(\bar P_{T_1}\le P_+\) and \(\kappa\bar P_{T_1}\le\ln2\). A discounted bound comes second. Let \(\mathfrak d_t\equiv P'_t-P_t\), so \(\mathfrak d_{T_1}=0\). By the mean value theorem, \(\mathcal P\left(P'_t\right)-\mathcal P\left(P_t\right)=\mathcal P'\left(\check P_t\right)\mathfrak d_t\) at a point \(\check P_t\) between \(P_t\) and \(P'_t\), hence in \(\left[0,P_+\right]\), where \(0<\mathcal P'=1-\theta-\theta'P<1+\rho\) because pollution does not tip there. So \(\left|\mathfrak d_{t+1}\right|\le\left(1+\rho\right)\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|+\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}\), and since \(\beta\left(1+\rho\right)=1\), induction gives \[
\beta^{t-T_1}\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|\;\le\;\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}\sum_{r\ge1}\beta^r\;=\;\bar d_{T_1}\equiv\frac{\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}}{\rho} .
\] As \(\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|\le P_+\) too, \(\beta^{t-T_1}\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|\le\min\left\{\bar d_{T_1},\beta^{t-T_1}P_+\right\}\). Let \(J\) be the least integer \(j\ge0\) with \(\beta^jP_+\le\bar d_{T_1}\), so \(J\le1+\ln^+\left(P_+/\bar d_{T_1}\right)/\ln\left(1+\rho\right)\) with \(\ln^+\equiv\max\left\{0,\ln\right\}\). The first \(J\) terms are at most \(\bar d_{T_1}\) each and the rest form a geometric tail, so \[
\sum_{t\ge T_1}\beta^{t-T_1}\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|\;\le\;\bar d_{T_1}\left[J+\frac{1+\rho}{\rho}\right] .
\] Since \(v'\) is increasing, the mean value theorem on \(\left[0,P_+\right]\) gives \(\left|v\left(P'_t\right)-v\left(P_t\right)\right|\le v'\left(P_+\right)\left|\mathfrak d_t\right|\) for \(t\ge T_1\).

Step 4: consumption. At \(t\ge T_1\) the goods constraints of \(z'\) and \(z\) differ in output, in gross formation, \(G'_t-G_t=Q_{t+1}-\left(1-\delta\right)Q_t\), and in the handling cost; the extraction and exploration costs agree. With \(C^W_t\ge0\), \(C^{W\prime}_t=\left[c^c\left(t\right)+c^T\left(1,t\right)\right]\mu\mathcal W'_t\le c^{\mathrm{full}}\mu\mathcal W'_t\), \(Q_t\ge0\) and \(Q_{t+1}\le K^{R\prime}_{t+1}=x'_{t+1}\mu\mathcal W'_{t+1}\), \[
C'_t\;\ge\;C_t+\left(Y'_t-Y_t\right)-\mathfrak s_tC_t,
\qquad
\mathfrak s_t\equiv\frac{x'_{t+1}\mu\mathcal W'_{t+1}+c^{\mathrm{full}}\mu\mathcal W'_t}{C_t}\quad\left(t\ge T_1\right),
\] and at \(T_1-1\), where only investment and consumption change, \(C'_{T_1-1}=C_{T_1-1}-Q_{T_1}\ge\left(1-\mathfrak s_{T_1-1}\right)C_{T_1-1}\) with \(\mathfrak s_{T_1-1}\equiv x'_{T_1}\mu\mathcal W_{T_1}/C_{T_1-1}\). For output, \(A_t\) and \(B_t\) are common to the two paths and \(K^{Y\prime}_t\ge K^Y_t\), so \[
\frac{Y'_t}{Y_t}=e^{-\kappa\left(P'_t-P_t\right)}\left(\frac{K^{Y\prime}_t}{K^Y_t}\right)^{\beta_K}\left(\frac{R'_t}{R_t}\right)^{\gamma}\;\ge\;e^{-\kappa\bar\delta}\left(\frac{R'_t}{R_t}\right)^{\gamma},
\] with \(\bar\delta\equiv0\) in case (b), by (b5), and \(\bar\delta\equiv\bar P_{T_1}\) in case (a), by (a4). Hence the consumption ratio \(\mathfrak c_t\equiv C'_t/C_t\) satisfies, for \(t\ge T_1\), \[
\mathfrak c_t\;\ge\;1+\frac{Y_t}{C_t}\left[e^{-\kappa\bar\delta}\left(\frac{R'_t}{R_t}\right)^{\gamma}-1\right]-\mathfrak s_t .
\]
The cost share vanishes. Let \(\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\equiv\sup_{t\ge T_1-1}\mathfrak s_t+\bar o\kappa\bar\delta\). In case (b), by (b2), (b3) and \(C_t\ge\left(1+g-\upsilon\right)^{t-T_1}C_{T_1}\ge\left(1+g/2\right)^{t-T_1}C_{T_1}\), \[
\mathfrak s_t\;\le\;\mu\bar w_b\frac{\mathcal W_{T_1}}{C_{T_1}}\cdot\frac{\xi^{-1}\left[b_0+b_1\left(t+1-T_1\right)\right]+c^{\mathrm{full}}}{\left(1+g/2\right)^{t-T_1}}\;\le\;\mu\bar w_b\,\mathfrak m_b\frac{\mathcal W_{T_1}}{C_{T_1}},
\qquad
\mathfrak m_b\equiv\sup_{j\ge0}\frac{\xi^{-1}\left[b_0+b_1\left(j+1\right)\right]+c^{\mathrm{full}}}{\left(1+g/2\right)^{j}},
\] finite because \(g>0\) and the numerator is affine in \(j\); and \(\mathfrak s_{T_1-1}\le\mu\xi^{-1}b_0\left(1+g+\upsilon\right)\mathcal W_{T_1}/C_{T_1}\). In case (a), by (a2) and \(1-\nu'<1+g-\upsilon\), \(\mathfrak s_t\le\left(x^\circ+c^{\mathrm{full}}\right)\mu\bar w_a\mathcal W_{T_1}/C_{T_1}\) and \(\mathfrak s_{T_1-1}\le x^\circ\mu\left(1+g+\upsilon\right)\mathcal W_{T_1}/C_{T_1}\), while \(\bar P_{T_1}\to0\) by (a4). Every constant here is independent of \(T_1\), and \(\mathcal W_{T_1}/C_{T_1}\to0\) by Lemma Z(b), so \(\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\to0\).
The lag. Let \(m\ge1\) be the least integer with \(\left(c_R\vartheta^m\right)^{\gamma}\ge2\left(1+1/\underline o\right)\); it exists because \(\vartheta>1\), and it does not depend on \(T_1\). Take \(T_1\) large enough that \(\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\le\frac12\). Then:

at \(t=T_1-1\), \(\mathfrak c_t\ge1-\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\);
at \(t\ge T_1\), \(R'_t\ge R_t\) by (b4) or (a3), so the bracket is at least \(e^{-\kappa\bar\delta}-1\ge-\kappa\bar\delta\); if it is negative, \(Y_t/C_t\le\bar o\) gives \(\mathfrak c_t\ge1-\bar o\kappa\bar\delta-\mathfrak s_t\ge1-\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\), and if it is nonnegative, \(\mathfrak c_t\ge1-\mathfrak s_t\ge1-\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\);
at \(t\ge T_1+m\), \(e^{-\kappa\bar\delta}\ge\frac12\) and \(R'_t/R_t\ge c_R\vartheta^m\) make the bracket at least \(1/\underline o\), so \(\mathfrak c_t\ge1+\underline o/\underline o-\mathfrak s_t\ge\frac32\).

In particular \(C'_t\ge\frac12C_t>0\) at every \(t\ge T_1-1\).
Step 5: feasibility. Through \(T_1-2\) the controls are those of \(z\), so the states agree through \(T_1-1\). At \(T_1-1\) investment and consumption change by \(+Q_{T_1}\) and \(-Q_{T_1}\), which keeps the goods constraint, and \(C'_{T_1-1}>0\) by step 4. From \(T_1\) on, the goods constraint holds by the definition of \(C'_t\), with \(C'_t>0\) by step 4, and the material constraints hold by step 1; \(K'_t-K^{R\prime}_t=K^{Y\prime}_t\ge K^Y_t\ge0\); and gross formation carries no sign restriction. From \(T_1-1\) on, \(K'_{t+1}=K_{t+1}+Q_{t+1}\ge0\). With \(\phi^I=0\) the intensity condition reads \(R=\Omega\mathcal D\), and it holds with \(\Omega'_t=R'_t/\mathcal D'_t\), nonnegative and finite, once \(\mathcal D'_t>0\) for \(t\ge T_1-1\). On \(z\), \(R_t=\Omega_t\mathcal D_t>0\) with \(\Omega_t\ge0\), so \(\mathcal D_t>0\) for \(t\ge T_0\). Every term of \(\mathcal D\) is nonnegative, and term by term \(\mathcal D'_t\ge\frac12\mathcal D_t\): consumption is at least half that of \(z\) by step 4; output is at least half, since \(Y'_t\ge e^{-\kappa\bar\delta}Y_t\ge\frac12Y_t\) for \(t\ge T_1\) and \(Y'_{T_1-1}=Y_{T_1-1}\); the extraction and exploration costs are those of \(z\); and the handling cost is at least that of \(z\), \(C^{W\prime}_t=\left[c^c\left(t\right)+c^T\left(1,t\right)\right]\mu\mathcal W'_t\ge\left[c^c\left(t\right)\varpi_t+c^T\left(\varpi_t,t\right)\right]\mu\mathcal W_t=C^W_t\), because \(c^T\) increases in \(\varpi\) and \(\mathcal W'_t\ge\mathcal W_t\) by (b1) or (a1), with equality at \(T_1-1\). So \(z'\) is feasible.
Step 6: the value. For every \(\eta>0\) let \(\mathfrak u\left(y\right)\equiv\left(y^{1-\eta}-1\right)/\left(1-\eta\right)\) for \(\eta\ne1\) and \(\mathfrak u\left(y\right)\equiv\ln y\) at \(\eta=1\), so that \(u\left(yC\right)-u\left(C\right)=C^{1-\eta}\,\mathfrak u\left(y\right)\). \(\mathfrak u\) is increasing and concave with \(\mathfrak u\left(1\right)=0\) and \(\mathfrak u'\left(y\right)=y^{-\eta}\), so on \(\left[\frac12,1\right]\) concavity gives \(\mathfrak u\left(y\right)\ge-\mathfrak u'\left(y\right)\left(1-y\right)\ge-2^{\eta}\left(1-y\right)\), and \(\mathfrak u\ge0\) on \(\left[1,\infty\right)\). By step 4, \(\mathfrak u\left(\mathfrak c_t\right)\ge-2^{\eta}\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\) for \(t\ge T_1-1\) and \(\mathfrak u\left(\mathfrak c_t\right)\ge\mathfrak u\left(\frac32\right)>0\) for \(t\ge T_1+m\). The two paths agree in consumption before \(T_1-1\) and in pollution through \(T_1\), so their partial sums of value differ by \[
\sum_{t=T_1-1}^{T}\pi_t\,\mathfrak u\left(\mathfrak c_t\right)-\sum_{t=T_1}^{T}\beta^t\left[v\left(P'_t\right)-v\left(P_t\right)\right] .
\] The first sum has terms bounded below by \(-2^{\eta}\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\pi_t\), summable by Lemma Z(c), so it converges in \(\left(-\infty,+\infty\right]\); the second converges absolutely, both paths’ pollution lying in \(\left[0,\bar P\right]\), where \(v\) is bounded; and the value of \(z\) is finite. So the value of \(z'\) exists in \(\left(-\infty,+\infty\right]\), and \(U_0\left(z'\right)-U_0\left(z\right)\) is the limit of the display as \(T\to\infty\). Bound the first sum below by \(-2^{\eta}\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\pi_t\) on \(T_1-1\le t<T_1+m\) and by \(\mathfrak u\left(\frac32\right)\pi_t\) on \(t\ge T_1+m\), and use Lemma Z(c) from \(s=T_1-1\ge T_0\): \(\pi_{T_1-1}\le\pi_{T_1}/\left(\Pi-\upsilon\right)\), \(\sum_{t\ge T_1}\pi_t\le\pi_{T_1}/\left(1-\Pi-\upsilon\right)\) and \(\sum_{t\ge T_1+m}\pi_t\ge\pi_{T_1}\left(\Pi-\upsilon\right)^m/\left(1-\Pi+\upsilon\right)\). The pollution sum is nonpositive in case (b), by (b5) and \(v'>0\), and in case (a) at most \(\beta^{T_1}v'\left(P_+\right)\bar d_{T_1}\left[J+\left(1+\rho\right)/\rho\right]\), by (a4). Dividing by \(\pi_{T_1}=\beta^{T_1}C_{T_1}^{1-\eta}\), \[
\frac{U_0\left(z'\right)-U_0\left(z\right)}{\beta^{T_1}C_{T_1}^{1-\eta}}
\;\ge\;
\underbrace{\mathfrak u\left(\tfrac32\right)\frac{\left(\Pi-\upsilon\right)^m}{1-\Pi+\upsilon}}_{\text{gain}}
-\underbrace{2^{\eta}\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\left[\frac1{\Pi-\upsilon}+\frac1{1-\Pi-\upsilon}\right]}_{\text{cost}}
-\underbrace{\frac{v'\left(P_+\right)\mu\bar w_a}{\rho}\,\mathcal W_{T_1}C_{T_1}^{\eta-1}\left[J+\frac{1+\rho}{\rho}\right]}_{\text{pollution, case (a)}} .
\] The gain is positive and independent of \(T_1\), and the cost tends to zero with \(\bar{\mathfrak s}_{T_1}\). In case (a), \(\ln^+\left(P_+/\bar d_{T_1}\right)\le\ln^+\left[\rho P_+/\left(\mu\bar w_a\right)\right]+\ln^+\left(1/\mathcal W_{T_1}\right)\), and Lemma Z(d) gives \(\mathcal W_{T_1}\ge\left(1-\nu-\upsilon\right)^{T_1-T_0}\mathcal W_{T_0}\), so \(J\) grows at most linearly in \(T_1\); the pollution term is then at most a constant times \(\left(1+T_1\right)\mathcal W_{T_1}C_{T_1}^{\eta-1}\), which tends to zero by Lemma Z(b). This is where the condition of (a) enters. So there is a date beyond which every switch date \(T_1\) gives \(U_0\left(z'\right)>U_0\left(z\right)\), the switch copying \(z\) until \(T_1-2\) and then treating all handled waste at a lower loss rate.

title: O.6 The entry condition into treatment
text:
The statement
Proposition 9 of the paper (the entry condition into treatment) states when the waste sector treats the flow it handles, at any setting of the instruments and on a candidate planner path, and what open access, the owned stockpile and a rising material price make of that test. This page proves it in full. Symbols are the paper’s, as on the notation page; a symbol the proof needs beyond them is defined where it is first used.
Proposition 9 (the entry condition into treatment). General primitives. At any date with a positive handled flow, a positive rental and a positive handling wedge \(P^W>0\), at any setting of the instruments and under either ownership regime:
We take the simplest route for the paper’s assumptions. Every item holds for general primitives, with no functional form. Items 1 to 3 are statements about one date, and only the planner’s clause of item 1 uses first-order conditions. What the statement and the proof take from Sections 2 and 4 and from Appendix A of the paper is restated in What the proof uses.

title: O.6 The entry condition into treatment
text:
What the proof uses
From Section 2 of the paper. Within a date we suppress the time argument and write \(a'\) for \(a_x\). We read the yield as continuous on \(\left[0,\infty\right)\) and twice differentiable on \(\left(0,\infty\right)\), as its derivatives presume. Then \(a'\) is positive and strictly decreasing, and it tends to zero at infinity, since a limit \(\ell>0\) would make \(a\left(x\right)\ge a\left(1\right)+\ell\left(x-1\right)\) unbounded; and \(a\) rises strictly to \(\bar a\), so \(a\left(x\right)<\bar a\). By the mean value theorem \(a\left(x\right)=a'\left(\xi\right)x\) for some \(\xi\in\left(0,x\right)\). So \(a\left(x\right)>a'\left(x\right)x\), and the slope of the yield at the origin, which Section 4.2 writes \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)\equiv\lim_{x\downarrow0}a\left(x\right)/x\), is also \(\lim_{x\downarrow0}a'\left(x\right)\), a limit in \(\left(0,\infty\right]\) as \(a'\) is positive and decreasing. The marginal recycling yield \(\alpha\left(x\right)\equiv a\left(x\right)-a'\left(x\right)x\) therefore has \(0<\alpha\left(x\right)\le a\left(x\right)\) for \(x>0\), and we set \(\alpha\left(0\right)\equiv0\). For a treated flow \(T>0\), \(\mathcal R\left(T,xT\right)=a\left(x\right)T\), and with none nothing is recovered, \(\mathcal R\left(0,K^R\right)=0\), the only value consistent with \(0\le\mathcal R\le\bar aT\). The collection charge \(c^c\) is positive; \(c^T\left(0\right)=c^{T\prime}\left(0\right)=0\), \(c^{T\prime}>0\) on \(\left(0,1\right]\) and \(c^{T\prime\prime}>0\), so \(c^{T\prime}\) increases strictly on \(\left[0,1\right]\) and \(c^T\left(\varpi\right)>0\) for \(\varpi>0\); both charges are nonincreasing in time. \(\Omega^j=\Omega\omega^j\ge0\), since \(\omega^j\ge0\) and \(\Omega\ge0\) in Problem 1. Output vanishes below the floor, so \(F_K=F_R=0\) where \(R<\bar R\), while where \(R\ge\bar R\), \(F_K=\mathcal F_K>0\) and \(F_R=\mathcal F_{R^e}>0\). Section 2.1 maintains, at the output function, “the Inada condition in capital, \(\mathcal F_K\to\infty\) as \(K^Y\to0\) at any \(R^e>0\)”.
From Section 4 of the paper. The gate fee \(\tau^W\) is what a generator pays to hand over a tonne of waste, the emission tax \(\tau^P\) is levied per tonne of \(\Xi\) on its emitter, \(z\) is the material-content price, and a unit of the final good put to the current use \(j\) costs the user price \(P^j\equiv1+\left(z+\tau^W\right)\Omega^j\) (Section 4.1). With \(p^R\) the price of a tonne of raw material and \(r^K\) the rental of capital, the final-goods sector’s first-order conditions are \(F_R\left[1-\left(z+\tau^W\right)\Omega^Y\right]=p^R-z\) and \(F_K\left[1-\left(z+\tau^W\right)\Omega^Y\right]=r^K\), and where \(N>0\) the mining sector’s extraction condition is \(p^R=P^NC^N_N+\tau^P\Omega^{N,S}+p^S\), with \(p^S\) the mine’s value of a tonne left in the ground. An idle date has \(Y=R=0\) and a zero rental (Definition 2); at every other date the final-goods sector operates and its two conditions hold.
The waste sector (Section 4.1) takes in the flow \(W_t\) at the fee, draws \(H_t=\mu\mathcal W_t\) from the waste stock, chooses the treated share \(\varpi_t\in\left[0,1\right]\) and the recycling capital \(K^R_t\ge0\), rented at \(r^K_t\), sells \(R^R_t=\mathcal R\left(\varpi_tH_t,K^R_t\right)\) at \(p^R_t\), buys the \(C^W_t=\left[c^c\varpi_t+c^T\left(\varpi_t\right)\right]H_t\) units of the final good its handling uses at \(P^W_t\), and pays the emission tax on \(\Xi^h_t\); \(\tilde p\equiv p^R+d^W\tau^P\) is its value of a recovered tonne. Where the stock is owned, the sector’s value \(J^W_t\) “is the fee on what it accepts, plus its operating profit, plus the discounted value of the stock it carries into the next period” (Section 4.1): the largest value, over \(W_t\ge0\) and the pair \(\left(\varpi_t,K^R_t\right)\), of its period cash flow plus \(J^W_{t+1}\left(\left(1-\mu\right)\mathcal W_t+W_t\right)/\left(1+r_{t+1}\right)\), with \(r\) the market interest rate; \(J^W\) is real-valued, the paper differentiating it to price the stock. Where nobody owns the stock, “since nobody values the stock, the waste sector chooses its treated share and recycling capital against its operating profit alone” (Section 4.2), a reason that holds whatever the instruments.
Under open access (Section 4.2) nobody owns the stock and \(\tau^W=\tau^P=z=0\), so every user price is one and, where the final-goods sector operates, \(p^R=F_R\) and \(r^K=F_K\). At the owned stockpile the stock is owned and \(\tau^P=z=0\), so \(P^W=1+\tau^W\Omega^W\) and, where the final-goods sector operates, \(p^R=F_R\left(1-\tau^W\Omega^Y\right)\) and \(r^K=F_K\left(1-\tau^W\Omega^Y\right)\). For \(r^K>0\) the recovery value of a treated tonne and the entry margin are (Section 4.2) \[
\mathcal G^{x}\!\left(\tilde p,r^K\right)\equiv\max_{x\ge0}\left[a\left(x\right)\tilde p-r^Kx\right],
\qquad
E\equiv\mathcal G^{x}\!\left(\tilde p,r^K\right)+\tau^P\left(1-d^W\right)-P^Wc^c ,
\] and \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}\) and \(E^{\mathrm{OS}}\) are \(E\) under open access and at the owned stockpile; “at a common \(\left(F_R,F_K,\Omega\right)\)” evaluates both at the same values of the three.
From Appendix A, through the shared page. The shared page of the long-run proofs restates the prices of Appendix A and the Lagrangian of Problem 1. We take from it that \(\lambda_t>0\) on a candidate, by (C); that the pair \(\left(\varpi,K^R\right)\) enters the period-\(t\) terms of the Lagrangian only as \(\beta^t\lambda_t\) times the braces \(\left\{Y-C^W-p^WR+\zeta\left[R-\Omega\left(\mathcal D+\phi^IG\right)\right]-p^P\Xi\right\}\), whose derivatives where \(\varpi H>0\) are \(a'\mathcal G^K-\tilde F_K\) in \(K^R\) and \(H\left\{\mathcal G^\varpi-\left[c^c+c^{T\prime}\left(\varpi\right)\right]\left(1+\zeta\Omega^W\right)\right\}\) in \(\varpi\); and the prices of (G), \(\Psi\equiv F_R\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)+\zeta\), \(\mathcal G^K\equiv\Psi-p^W+d^Wp^P\) and \(\mathcal G^\varpi=\alpha\mathcal G^K+\left(1-d^W\right)p^P\), with \(\tilde F_K\equiv F_K\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)\).
Appendix A states the conditions on the pair, (KR) and (T) where it is interior, as branch systems in which “each corner holds when its inequality goes the other way”; “\(F_R\) is \(\mathcal F_{R^e}\) at the prevailing \(R\ge\bar R\)” and “the conditions are evaluated on operating periods”. It notes that “The upper bound \(K^R\le K\) never binds, since \(F_K\to\infty\) as \(K^Y\to0\)”, the reason being Section 2.1’s Inada condition in capital, \(\mathcal F_K\to\infty\) as \(K^Y\to0\) at any \(R^e>0\), and adds: “At \(\varpi=0\) the ratio \(x=K^R/\left(\varpi H\right)\) is undefined, so entry into treatment and into recycling capital is one joint decision, tested over the best available pair \(\left(\varpi,x\right)\).” We read these first-order conditions as one requirement on the pair: at the candidate’s pair, with every other control and every multiplier held at the candidate’s values, the one-sided derivative of the braces is nonpositive in every direction \(\left(d\varpi,dK^R\right)\) along which the pair stays in \(\left[0,1\right]\times\left[0,K_t\right]\) for small steps, \(\mathcal F\) being differentiable at the date’s input, as the shared page’s derivatives presume. Where the pair is interior this is (KR) and (T), at a bound the inequality of its branch, and at \(\varpi=0\) the joint test.

title: O.6 The entry condition into treatment
text:
The recovery value
Lemma R. Let \(r>0\) and \(\tilde p\) be real. The maximum of \(f\left(x\right)\equiv a\left(x\right)\tilde p-rx\) over \(x\ge0\) is attained at exactly one point \(x^*\left(\tilde p,r\right)\): \(x^*>0\) with \(a'\left(x^*\right)\tilde p=r\) if \(\tilde p>0\) and \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)\tilde p>r\), and \(x^*=0\) otherwise. Its value is \(\mathcal G^x\left(\tilde p,r\right)=\alpha\left(x^*\right)\tilde p\), and:
(a) \(\mathcal G^x\ge0\), with \(\mathcal G^x>0\) if and only if \(x^*>0\);
(b) \(\mathcal G^x<\bar a\tilde p\) if \(\tilde p>0\);
(c) for \(s>0\), \(x^*\left(s\tilde p,sr\right)=x^*\left(\tilde p,r\right)\) and \(\mathcal G^x\left(s\tilde p,sr\right)=s\,\mathcal G^x\left(\tilde p,r\right)\).

Proof. \(f\) is continuous on \(\left[0,\infty\right)\) with \(f\left(0\right)=0\). If \(\tilde p\le0\), \(a\tilde p\) is nonincreasing and \(-rx\) strictly decreasing, so \(f\) falls strictly and \(x^*=0\). If \(\tilde p>0\), \(f'\left(x\right)=a'\left(x\right)\tilde p-r\) is continuous and strictly decreasing on \(\left(0,\infty\right)\), with limit \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)\tilde p-r\) at the origin and \(-r<0\) at infinity. If \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)\tilde p>r\), exactly one \(x^*>0\) has \(f'\left(x^*\right)=0\), and \(f\) rises strictly on \(\left[0,x^*\right]\) and falls strictly on \(\left[x^*,\infty\right)\); otherwise \(f'<0\) on \(\left(0,\infty\right)\) and \(f\) falls strictly from \(x=0\). Either way the maximiser is unique. At an interior \(x^*\), \(r=a'\left(x^*\right)\tilde p\) gives \(f\left(x^*\right)=\left[a\left(x^*\right)-a'\left(x^*\right)x^*\right]\tilde p=\alpha\left(x^*\right)\tilde p\); at \(x^*=0\) both sides are zero.

\(\mathcal G^x\ge f\left(0\right)=0\). If \(x^*>0\), then \(\tilde p>0\) and \(\alpha\left(x^*\right)>0\), so \(\mathcal G^x>0\); if \(x^*=0\), \(\mathcal G^x=0\). (b) \(\alpha\left(x^*\right)\le a\left(x^*\right)<\bar a\). (c) \(f\) at \(\left(s\tilde p,sr\right)\) is \(s\) times \(f\) at \(\left(\tilde p,r\right)\), so it has the same maximiser and \(s\) times the maximum.

section: The waste sector’s choice at a date
text:
The waste sector’s choice at a date
Lemma H. Take a date with \(H>0\), \(r^K>0\) and \(P^W>0\), any setting of the instruments and either ownership regime.
(a) The waste sector’s pair maximises over \(\left[0,1\right]\times\left[0,\infty\right)\) its operating profit, the part of its period cash flow that the pair moves, \[
\Pi^W\!\left(\varpi,K^R\right)\equiv\tilde p\,\mathcal R\left(\varpi H,K^R\right)+\tau^P\left(1-d^W\right)\varpi H-P^W\left[c^c\varpi+c^T\!\left(\varpi\right)\right]H-r^KK^R-\tau^PH .
\]
(b) This problem has exactly one solution, \(\left(\varpi^*,\varpi^*x^*H\right)\), with \(x^*=x^*\left(\tilde p,r^K\right)\) of Lemma R and \(\varpi^*\) the unique maximiser over \(\left[0,1\right]\) of \(\hat\pi\left(\varpi\right)\equiv\varpi E-P^Wc^T\!\left(\varpi\right)-\tau^P\).
(c) \(\varpi^*=0\) if and only if \(E\le0\), and \(\varpi^*=1\) if and only if \(E\ge P^Wc^{T\prime}\!\left(1\right)\).

Proof. 

The period cash flow is \(\tau^WW+p^RR^R-P^WC^W-r^KK^R-\tau^P\Xi^h\). With \(\Xi^h=\left[1-\varpi+d^W\varpi\left(1-a\right)\right]H=\left(1-\varpi+d^W\varpi\right)H-d^WR^R\) it is \(\tau^WW+\Pi^W\left(\varpi,K^R\right)\). Where the stock is owned, the sector’s choice at date \(t\) maximises \(\Pi^W\left(\varpi,K^R\right)+\tau^W_tW_t+J^W_{t+1}\left(\left(1-\mu\right)\mathcal W_t+W_t\right)/\left(1+r_{t+1}\right)\). The handled flow is fixed when the period opens and the pair is not in the transition, so the pair enters only through \(\Pi^W\); at a solution the other two terms are a real number, and a pair with a larger \(\Pi^W\), \(W_t\) kept, would raise the value. Where nobody owns the stock, the sector chooses the pair against \(\Pi^W\) alone.
Fix \(\varpi\in\left(0,1\right]\). As \(\varpi H>0\), \(K^R=x\varpi H\) maps \(x\ge0\) one to one onto \(K^R\ge0\), and \(\mathcal R\left(\varpi H,x\varpi H\right)=a\left(x\right)\varpi H\), so \[
\Pi^W\!\left(\varpi,x\varpi H\right)=\varpi H\left[a\left(x\right)\tilde p-r^Kx\right]+\tau^P\left(1-d^W\right)\varpi H-P^W\left[c^c\varpi+c^T\!\left(\varpi\right)\right]H-\tau^PH ,
\] which by Lemma R is largest exactly at \(x=x^*\), with value \(H\hat\pi\left(\varpi\right)\). At \(\varpi=0\) nothing is recovered and \(\Pi^W\left(0,K^R\right)=-r^KK^R-\tau^PH\), largest exactly at \(K^R=0\), with value \(H\hat\pi\left(0\right)\). So for every \(\varpi\) the largest \(\Pi^W\) is \(H\hat\pi\left(\varpi\right)\), attained only at \(K^R=\varpi x^*H\). As \(P^W>0\) and \(c^T\) is strictly convex, \(\hat\pi\) is continuous and strictly concave, with a unique maximiser \(\varpi^*\) on \(\left[0,1\right]\). Every pair has \(\Pi^W\left(\varpi,K^R\right)\le H\hat\pi\left(\varpi\right)\le H\hat\pi\left(\varpi^*\right)=\Pi^W\left(\varpi^*,\varpi^*x^*H\right)\), and as \(H>0\) one of the two inequalities is strict unless \(\varpi=\varpi^*\) and \(K^R=\varpi^*x^*H\).
\(\hat\pi\left(\varpi\right)-\hat\pi\left(0\right)=\varpi E-P^Wc^T\!\left(\varpi\right)\). If \(E\le0\) it is negative for \(\varpi>0\), as \(c^T\left(\varpi\right)>0\), so \(\varpi^*=0\). If \(E>0\) it equals \(\varpi\left[E-P^Wc^T\!\left(\varpi\right)/\varpi\right]\), positive for small \(\varpi>0\) since \(c^T\!\left(\varpi\right)/\varpi\to c^{T\prime}\!\left(0\right)=0\), so \(\varpi^*>0\). On \(\left(0,1\right]\) the derivative of \(\hat\pi\), \(E-P^Wc^{T\prime}\!\left(\varpi\right)\), falls strictly. If \(E\ge P^Wc^{T\prime}\!\left(1\right)\) it is positive on \(\left(0,1\right)\), \(\hat\pi\) rises strictly on \(\left[0,1\right]\) and \(\varpi^*=1\); if \(E<P^Wc^{T\prime}\!\left(1\right)\) it is negative at \(\varpi=1\), so some \(\varpi<1\) does better than \(1\).

title: O.6 The entry condition into treatment
text:
Proof of Proposition 9

Proof. Item 1, the waste sector. By Lemma H, whenever the sector solves its problem its pair is \(\left(\varpi^*,\varpi^*x^*H\right)\): the treated share is unique, \(\varpi=0\) exactly when \(E\le0\), and \(\varpi=1\) exactly when \(E\ge P^Wc^{T\prime}\!\left(1\right)\). When \(E>0\), \(\varpi>0\) and \(K^R=x^*\varpi H\), so the intensity \(K^R/\left(\varpi H\right)\) is \(x^*\).
Item 1, a candidate planner path. Take a candidate and a date \(t\) with \(H_t>0\), \(\tilde F_{K,t}>0\) and \(1+\zeta_t\Omega^W_t>0\). As \(F_K\ne0\), \(R_t\ge\bar R\). And \(K^Y_t>0\), so \(K^R_t<K_t\), as Appendix A’s sentence on the upper bound states; Section 2.1’s Inada clause is its reason, \(\tilde F_{K,t}\) being a real number while \(\mathcal F_K\to\infty\) as \(K^Y\to0\) at any \(R^e>0\). By Lemma R at \(\left(\mathcal G^K_t,\tilde F_{K,t}\right)\), \(E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t=\max_{x\ge0}\Upsilon_t\left(x\right)\), with \[
\Upsilon_t\left(x\right)\equiv a\left(x\right)\mathcal G^K_t-x\tilde F_{K,t}+\left(1-d^W\right)p^P_t-\left(1+\zeta_t\Omega^W_t\right)c^c .
\]
No treatment implies \(E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t\le0\). Let \(\varpi_t=0\). Then \(K^R_t=0\): with no treated flow nothing is recovered, so \(K^R\) moves the braces only through \(Y=F\left(K-K^R,R,P,t\right)\), directly and in \(\mathcal D\), at the rate \(-\tilde F_{K,t}<0\), and lowering a positive \(K^R_t\) would raise them, against the requirement. At the corner \(\left(0,0\right)\), \(K_t=K^Y_t>0\), so for every \(x\ge0\) the direction \(\left(1,xH_t\right)\) is feasible, and every feasible direction with \(d\varpi>0\) is a positive multiple of one of them. Along \(\left(\varpi,K^R\right)=\left(\epsilon,\epsilon xH_t\right)\), \(\epsilon\downarrow0\), the treated flow \(\epsilon H_t\) is positive, so \(R^R=\epsilon a\left(x\right)H_t\), \(R=N_t+R^R\ge\bar R\), \(K^Y=K_t-\epsilon xH_t\), \(C^W=\left[c^c\epsilon+c^T\left(\epsilon\right)\right]H_t\) and \(\Xi^h=\left[1-\left(1-d^W\right)\epsilon-d^Wa\left(x\right)\epsilon\right]H_t\); up to terms the pair does not move, the braces are \(\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)Y-\left(1+\zeta\Omega^W\right)C^W+\left(\zeta-p^W\right)R-p^P\Xi^h\). Their derivative at \(\epsilon=0^+\) is, with \(c^{T\prime}\left(0\right)=0\) and (G), \[
H_t\Big\{a\left(x\right)\left[F_R\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)+\zeta-p^W+d^Wp^P\right]-xF_K\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)+\left(1-d^W\right)p^P-\left(1+\zeta\Omega^W\right)c^c\Big\}\Big|_t=H_t\,\Upsilon_t\left(x\right).
\] The requirement on the pair makes it nonpositive for every \(x\ge0\), so \(E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t\le0\).
\(E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t\le0\) implies no treatment. Suppose \(\varpi_t>0\), and let \(x_t\equiv K^R_t/\left(\varpi_tH_t\right)\). Lowering \(\varpi\) is feasible, and with the shared page’s derivative in \(\varpi\) the requirement gives (T), or its corner at \(\varpi_t=1\), as \(\mathcal G^\varpi_t\ge\left(1+\zeta_t\Omega^W_t\right)\left[c^c+c^{T\prime}\left(\varpi_t\right)\right]\). If \(K^R_t>0\), lowering \(K^R\) is feasible and gives \(a'\left(x_t\right)\mathcal G^K_t\ge\tilde F_{K,t}\), so \(\alpha\left(x_t\right)\mathcal G^K_t\le a\left(x_t\right)\mathcal G^K_t-x_t\tilde F_{K,t}\); if \(K^R_t=0\), \(\alpha\left(x_t\right)=0\). Either way \(\alpha\left(x_t\right)\mathcal G^K_t\le\mathcal G^x\left(\mathcal G^K_t,\tilde F_{K,t}\right)\), by the definition of the maximum and Lemma R(a), and with (G) \[
E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t\;\ge\;\mathcal G^\varpi_t-\left(1+\zeta_t\Omega^W_t\right)c^c\;\ge\;\left(1+\zeta_t\Omega^W_t\right)c^{T\prime}\!\left(\varpi_t\right)\;>\;0 ,
\] since \(c^{T\prime}>0\) on \(\left(0,1\right]\), against \(E^{\mathrm{pl}}_t\le0\).
Item 2. Under open access, at a date with a positive rental the final-goods sector operates, so \(\tilde p=p^R=F_R\), \(r^K=F_K>0\), \(\tau^P=0\) and \(P^W=1\); then \(R\ge\bar R\), as \(F_K=0\) below the floor, and \(F_R>0\). Lemma R gives \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}=\mathcal G^x\left(F_R,F_K\right)-c^c=\alpha\left(x^*\right)F_R-c^c\), with \(x^*\) interior and \(a'\left(x^*\right)F_R=F_K\) exactly when \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)F_R>F_K\). By item 1 the economy treats only if \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}>0\), and by Lemma R(b) \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}<\bar aF_R-c^c\), so it treats only if \(\bar aF_R>c^c\). Where it extracts, the extraction condition with \(P^N=1\), \(\tau^P=0\) and \(p^R=F_R\) reads \(F_R=C^N_N+p^S\).
Item 3. At a date with a positive rental the final-goods sector operates, and at the owned stockpile \(\tau^P=z=0\), so \(\tilde p=p^R=sF_R\) and \(r^K=sF_K\), with \(s\equiv1-\tau^W\Omega^Y\ge1\) as the fee is nonpositive, and \(P^W=1+\tau^W\Omega^W\). The positive rental gives \(F_K>0\), so \(R\ge\bar R\) and \(F_R>0\). By Lemma R(c) the intensity \(x^*\left(sF_R,sF_K\right)\) is open access’s \(x^*\left(F_R,F_K\right)\) and \(\mathcal G^x\left(sF_R,sF_K\right)=s\,\alpha\left(x^*\right)F_R\), so \(E^{\mathrm{OS}}=s\,\alpha\left(x^*\right)F_R-\left(1+\tau^W\Omega^W\right)c^c\). Subtracting \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}=\alpha\left(x^*\right)F_R-c^c\) at the same \(\left(F_R,F_K,\Omega\right)\) gives the identity. Each of \(-\tau^W\), \(\alpha\left(x^*\right)\), \(F_R\), \(\Omega^Y\), \(\Omega^W\) and \(c^c\) is nonnegative, and so is the difference. It is positive when \(\tau^W<0\) and the bracket is positive, that is when \(\Omega^W>0\), as \(c^c>0\), or when \(\Omega^Y>0\) and \(\alpha\left(x^*\right)>0\), which by Lemma R(a) holds exactly when \(x^*>0\).
Item 4. Of an open-access path we use only that at every date the waste sector chooses its pair against its operating profit at open access’s prices. The proposition speaks of dates with a positive rental, at which the final-goods sector operates, so \(\tilde p=F_{R,t}\), \(r^K=F_{K,t}>0\), \(\tau^P=0\) and \(P^W=1\). As \(F_{R,t}\to\infty\), \(F_{R,t}>0\) from some date on, and when \(\bar R>0\) every such date has a positive rental: there \(R_t\ge\bar R>0\), so the date is not idle and \(r^K=F_{K,t}>0\). At a date with a positive rental and \(F_{R,t}>0\), and for any \(\bar x>0\), the definition of the maximum, a yield nondecreasing and a collection charge nonincreasing in time give \[
E^{\mathrm{OA}}_t\;\ge\;a\left(\bar x,t\right)F_{R,t}-\bar xF_{K,t}-c^c\left(t\right)\;\ge\;F_{R,t}\left[a\left(\bar x,0\right)-\bar x\,\frac{F_{K,t}}{F_{R,t}}\right]-c^c\left(0\right) .
\] The bracket tends to \(a\left(\bar x,0\right)>0\) and \(F_{R,t}\) diverges, so \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}_t\to+\infty\) along the dates with a positive rental, and there is a date \(T_e\) after which \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}_t>0\) at each of them. At such a date with \(H_t>0\), item 1 gives \(\varpi_t>0\); as \(\tau^P=0\), \(\mathcal G^x=E^{\mathrm{OA}}_t+c^c\left(t\right)>0\), so \(x^*>0\) by Lemma R(a) and \(K^R_t=x^*\varpi_tH_t>0\). With \(W_t\ge0\) and \(\mu<1\), \(\mathcal W_{t+1}\ge\left(1-\mu\right)\mathcal W_t\), so a positive waste stock stays positive, and from the later of \(T_e\) and the first date at which the stock is positive the sector treats and rents recycling capital at every date with a positive rental. The marginal treatment cost at full treatment is \(P^Wc^{T\prime}\left(1,t\right)=c^{T\prime}\left(1,t\right)\); adding the collection charge, which lies in \(\left(0,c^c\left(0\right)\right]\), does not change whether it is bounded. If \(c^{T\prime}\left(1,t\right)\le\bar c\) at every date, there is a date \(T'_e\) after which \(E^{\mathrm{OA}}_t\ge\bar c\) at each date with a positive rental, and item 1 gives \(\varpi_t=1\) at each such date with \(H_t>0\).

title: O.7 The sign of the gate fee without the emission tax
text:
The statement
Proposition 11 of the paper (the gate fee without the emission tax) states that where the owner of the waste stock pays no tax on what the stock emits, the private handling dividend is never negative and the gate fee never positive, and when each is strictly so. It also states that under a nonnegative emission tax a positive fee needs a later tax. This page proves it in full. Symbols are the paper’s, as on the notation page; a symbol the proof needs beyond them is defined where it is first used.
Proposition 11 (the gate fee without the emission tax). General primitives, with \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)<\infty\), positive user prices of handling and consumption along the path, the sector solving its problem, and the price of the waste stock equal to the forward sum of its dividends. At the owned stockpile without instruments, and at any setting with the stock owned and \(\tau^P=0\) at every date:
1. \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\ge0\) at every date \(s\), with \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s>0\) if and only if \(s\) is a treatment date;
2. \(\tau^W_t\le0\) at every date \(t\); for \(\mu<1\), \(\tau^W_t<0\) if and only if some later date is a treatment date, so that when treatment never ceases for good the fee is negative at every date, even before treatment begins; for \(\mu=1\), \(\tau^W_t<0\) if and only if \(t+1\) is a treatment date.
With the stock owned and \(\tau^P_s=0\) only at the dates \(s>t\), item 1 holds at every \(s>t\) and item 2 at \(t\). At any setting with the stock owned and a nonnegative emission tax, a positive fee at \(t\) requires a positive tax at some later date, and is guaranteed when nothing is treated after \(t\) and the tax is positive at some later date (\(t+1\) when \(\mu=1\)), the fee then being the discounted sum of the taxes the stock will pay, \[
\tau^W_t = \sum_{s>t}\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,s}\left(1-\mu\right)^{s-t-1}\mu\,\tau^P_s ,
\qquad
\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,s}\equiv\prod_{j=t+1}^{s}\left(1+r_j\right)^{-1} .
\]
We take the simplest route for the paper’s assumptions; it needs no functional form. Item 1 compares the waste sector’s choices at one date, at prices it takes as given, item 2 sums the dividends of a tonne in the stock, and of the other agents only the household’s first-order condition enters, through the discount factors. What the proof uses restates the terms of the statement.

title: O.7 The sign of the gate fee without the emission tax
text:
What the proof uses
From the paper’s model (Section 2). The handled flow is \(H_t=\mu\mathcal W_t\), with \(\mathcal W_{t+1}=\left(1-\mu\right)\mathcal W_t+W_t\) and \(\mu\in\left(0,1\right)\), \(\mu=1\) being the limiting case. Handling costs \(c^W\left(\varpi\right)\equiv c^c\varpi+c^T\left(\varpi\right)\) units of the final good per handled tonne, with \(c^c>0\), \(c^T\left(0\right)=c^{T\prime}\left(0\right)=0\) and \(c^{T\prime\prime}>0\), so \(c^T\) is strictly convex and nonnegative, \(c^W\left(0\right)=0\) and \(c^W\left(\varpi\right)>0\) at \(\varpi>0\). Recovered material is \(R^R=a\left(x\right)T\), with \(T\equiv\varpi H\), \(x\equiv K^R/T\), \(a\left(0\right)=0\), \(a_x>0\), \(a_{xx}<0\) and \(a\le\bar a\le1\); as \(0\le R^R\le\bar aT\), a treated flow of zero recovers nothing. The marginal yield \(\alpha\equiv a-a'x\) of Appendix A.3 lies between zero and \(a\) at \(x>0\), and \(\alpha\left(0\right)=0\) as the slope \(a'\!\left(0^+\right)\) is finite, so \(\alpha\in\left[0,\bar a\right]\) at every intensity. And \(u'>0\).
From the paper’s market economy (Section 4.1, Appendix C). Raw material sells at \(p^R\) per tonne, capital rents at \(r^K\), handing over a tonne of waste costs the gate fee \(\tau^W\), and the matter in the final good is priced at the material-content price \(z\). A unit of the final good put to a current use \(j\in\left\{Y,N,D,W,C\right\}\) costs its buyer the user price \(P^j\equiv1+\left(z+\tau^W\right)\Omega\omega^j\). The instruments are an emission tax \(\tau^P\) per tonne of \(\Xi\), levied on the agent that emits it, a discovery tax \(\tau^X\), and \(z\). Agents take the paths of prices, instruments, \(P\) and \(\Omega\) as given and discount at the market interest rate \(r\).
The waste sector owns \(\mathcal W\). It takes in the flow \(W\) at the fee, draws \(H=\mu\mathcal W\) from its stock, chooses the treated share \(\varpi\in\left[0,1\right]\) and the recycling capital \(K^R\ge0\) it rents at \(r^K\), sells \(R^R\) at \(p^R\), pays the emission tax on the emission \(\Xi^h\) of Section 2, and buys its handling input at \(P^W\). Its operating profit at \(t\), which Appendix C writes with \(\Xi^h\) substituted, is \[
\Pi^W_t\left(\varpi,K^R\right)\equiv p^R_t\,R^R-P^W_t\,c^W\left(\varpi\right)H_t-r^K_tK^R-\tau^P_t\,\Xi^h ,
\] \(R^R\) and \(\Xi^h\) being those of the pair at the flow \(H_t\). Its value \(J^W_t\left(\mathcal W_t\right)\) is the fee on what it accepts, plus its operating profit, plus the discounted value of the stock it carries into the next period, at its best choice: the maximum over \(W_t\ge0\), \(\varpi_t\in\left[0,1\right]\) and \(K^R_t\ge0\) of \(\tau^W_tW_t+\Pi^W_t+J^W_{t+1}\left(\mathcal W_{t+1}\right)/\left(1+r_{t+1}\right)\). Its valuation of a tonne taken in at \(t\) is \(p^{\mathcal W}_t\equiv\left(1+r_{t+1}\right)^{-1}\partial J^W_{t+1}/\partial\mathcal W_{t+1}\), and with the stock owned the gate fee is minus that valuation (Section 4.1),  \[
\tau^W_t=-p^{\mathcal W}_t ,
\tag{GF}
\] and the valuation follows the recursion of Section 4.1, with the private handling dividend \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}\) taken at the sector’s treated share and intensity:  \[
\left(1+r_{t+1}\right)p^{\mathcal W}_t=\mu\,h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t+1}+\left(1-\mu\right)p^{\mathcal W}_{t+1},
\qquad
h^{\mathrm{mkt}}\equiv\alpha\varpi\,p^R-P^Wc^W-\tau^P\left[1-\varpi\left(1-d^W\right)-d^W\alpha\varpi\right].
\tag{WS}
\] The owned stockpile has the stock owned and nothing else set (Section 4.2): without instruments, \(\tau^P=z=\tau^X=0\) at every date. A setting with the stock owned has (GF) and any instrument paths. The displaced mass \(\mathcal N\) is emitted by the mining sector (Definition 2), so it enters neither the waste sector’s cash flow nor its stock.
The market interest rate is the household’s: with \(\Lambda_t\) its multiplier on its budget, \(u'\left(C_t\right)=\Lambda_tP^C_t\) and \(1+r_{t+1}\equiv\Lambda_t/\left(\beta\Lambda_{t+1}\right)\) (Appendix C, the household’s conditions). With \(u'>0\) and \(P^C_t>0\), a hypothesis of the statement, \(\Lambda_t>0\) at every date, so \(1+r_{t+1}>0\) and \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,s}=\beta^{s-t}\Lambda_s/\Lambda_t>0\) for \(s>t\).
The problem per handled tonne. At a date with \(H_s>0\) the sector’s pair per tonne is \(\left(\varpi_s,k^R_s\right)\), with \(k^R_s\equiv K^R_s/H_s\), and \(x_s=k^R_s/\varpi_s\) at \(\varpi_s>0\). At a date with \(H_s=0\) the operating profit \(-r^K_sK^R_s\) does not depend on the share, and the intensity is undefined. There we read the sector’s choice per handled tonne, as the share and the intensity at which a tonne added to the stock would be handled, which is what the dividend prices. Write \(K^R=k^RH\). At a date \(s\) with \(\tau^P_s=0\), \(\Pi^W_s\left(\varpi,k^RH_s\right)=H_s\,\pi_s\left(\varpi,k^R\right)\), where \[
\pi_s\left(\varpi,k^R\right)\equiv p^R_s\,\varpi\,a\!\left(k^R/\varpi\right)-P^W_s\,c^W\left(\varpi\right)-r^K_sk^R\quad\left(\varpi>0\right),
\qquad
\pi_s\left(0,k^R\right)\equiv-r^K_sk^R ,
\] as \(R^R=\varpi H_s\,a\left(k^R/\varpi\right)\) at \(\varpi>0\) and \(R^R=0\) at \(\varpi=0\). Let \(\pi^*_s\equiv\sup\pi_s\) over \(\varpi\in\left[0,1\right]\) and \(k^R\ge0\). At \(H_s>0\) the sector’s pair maximises \(\Pi^W_s\) exactly when its pair per tonne maximises \(\pi_s\). At \(H_s=0\) the reading takes a maximiser \(\left(\varpi_s,k^R_s\right)\) of \(\pi_s\), with \(x_s\equiv k^R_s/\varpi_s\) at \(\varpi_s>0\), since \(\pi_s\) is what a tonne added to the stock would earn; that the sector solves its problem includes, at such a date, that \(\pi_s\) has a maximiser.
The terms of the statement. A treatment date is a date \(s\) at which the sector treats, \(\varpi_s>0\), with the share per tonne at \(H_s=0\). The sector solves its problem when at every date its choice attains the maximum defining \(J^W_t\). As the pair \(\left(\varpi_t,K^R_t\right)\) enters that maximum only through \(\Pi^W_t\), the next stock not depending on it, the pair then maximises \(\Pi^W_t\), as Appendix C states, and at a date \(s\) with \(\tau^P_s=0\) the pair per tonne maximises \(\pi_s\). The forward sum of its dividends is \(\sum_{s>t}w_{t,s}h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\), with the weights of the statement’s display, \[
w_{t,s}\equiv\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,s}\left(1-\mu\right)^{s-t-1}\mu\qquad\left(s>t\right),
\] the probability that a tonne taken in at \(t\) is handled at \(s\), times the discount factor to \(t\). With \(0^0\equiv1\), at \(\mu=1\) the only weight that is not zero is \(w_{t,t+1}=\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,t+1}\). It is the forward solution of (WS): dividing (WS) by \(1+r_{t+1}\) and substituting it into itself from \(t\) to \(n\) gives the partial sum to \(n\) plus \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,n}\left(1-\mu\right)^{n-t}p^{\mathcal W}_n\).

title: O.7 The sign of the gate fee without the emission tax
section: The dividend is the optimised profit per handled tonne
text:
The dividend is the optimised profit per handled tonne
Lemma H. At a date \(s\) with \(\tau^P_s=0\) and \(P^W_s>0\), at which the sector solves its problem, \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s=\pi^*_s\ge0\), and \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s>0\) if and only if \(s\) is a treatment date.

Proof. Dumping is free. The pair \(\left(0,0\right)\) is feasible with \(\pi_s\left(0,0\right)=0\), so \(\pi^*_s\ge0\). The pair per tonne \(\left(\varpi_s,k^R_s\right)\) attains \(\pi^*_s\), which needs \(r^K_s\ge0\), since at \(r^K_s<0\) the profit \(\pi_s\left(0,k^R\right)=-r^K_sk^R\) grows without bound. At \(\tau^P_s=0\) the dividend is \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s=\alpha_s\varpi_sp^R_s-P^W_sc^W\left(\varpi_s\right)\).
Without treatment. Let \(\varpi_s=0\). Then \(\pi^*_s=-r^K_sk^R_s\le0\), so \(\pi^*_s=0\). Both terms of \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\) are zero: the first because \(\varpi_s=0\) and \(\alpha\in\left[0,\bar a\right]\), whatever value the undefined intensity gives it, the second as \(c^W\left(0\right)=0\). So \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s=0=\pi^*_s\).
Treatment leaves a rent. Let \(\varpi_s>0\) and \(\ell\in\left(0,1\right)\). Scaling the pair by \(\ell\) keeps its intensity, so revenue, collection cost and rent scale by \(\ell\), and \[
\pi_s\left(\ell\varpi_s,\ell k^R_s\right)-\ell\,\pi^*_s=P^W_s\left[\ell\,c^T\left(\varpi_s\right)-c^T\left(\ell\varpi_s\right)\right]>0 ,
\] by \(P^W_s>0\) and the strict convexity of \(c^T\) with \(c^T\left(0\right)=0\). Were \(\pi^*_s=0\), the feasible pair at \(\ell=\tfrac12\) would earn more than \(\pi^*_s\). So \(\pi^*_s>0\).
The rent is the dividend. Still with \(\varpi_s>0\): \(\pi_s\left(\varpi_s,0\right)=-P^W_sc^W\left(\varpi_s\right)<0\), since \(a\left(0\right)=0\), \(P^W_s>0\) and \(c^W\left(\varpi_s\right)>0\), so \(k^R_s>0\) and \(x_s\in\left(0,\infty\right)\). As \(k^R_s\) is an interior maximiser of \(k^R\mapsto\pi_s\left(\varpi_s,k^R\right)\), whose derivative is \(p^R_sa'\left(k^R/\varpi_s\right)-r^K_s\), we have \(p^R_sa'\left(x_s\right)=r^K_s\), the capital margin of Section 4.1 at \(\tau^P=0\). With \(a=\alpha+a'x\), \(\varpi_sa\left(x_s\right)=\alpha_s\varpi_s+a'\left(x_s\right)k^R_s\), so \[
\pi^*_s=\alpha_s\varpi_sp^R_s-P^W_sc^W\left(\varpi_s\right)+k^R_s\left[p^R_sa'\left(x_s\right)-r^K_s\right]=h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s .
\] In both cases \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s=\pi^*_s\), positive exactly when \(\varpi_s>0\). The cases apply to every maximiser of \(\pi_s\), so either every maximiser treats or none does: whether \(s\) is a treatment date does not depend on the one the sector picks.

title: O.7 The sign of the gate fee without the emission tax
text:
Proof of Proposition 11

Proof. Step 1: item 2 at a date \(t\) with \(\tau^P_s=0\) at every \(s>t\). Lemma H applies at every \(s>t\), as \(P^W_s>0\) and the sector solves its problem, so \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\ge0\), positive exactly when \(s\) is a treatment date. By the hypothesis on the price of the waste stock, \(p^{\mathcal W}_t=\sum_{s>t}w_{t,s}h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\), a sum of nonnegative terms, which is nonnegative and positive exactly when one of its terms is. When \(\mu<1\) every weight is positive, as \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}_{t,s}>0\) and \(\mu>0\), so \(p^{\mathcal W}_t>0\) exactly when some \(s>t\) is a treatment date; at \(\mu=1\) the only positive weight is \(w_{t,t+1}\), so \(p^{\mathcal W}_t>0\) exactly when \(t+1\) is one. By (GF), \(\tau^W_t=-p^{\mathcal W}_t\le0\), negative on the same conditions. The argument uses \(\tau^P\) at the dates after \(t\) only, which with Lemma H at each \(s>t\) is the sentence of the statement on \(\tau^P_s=0\) only at the dates \(s>t\).
Step 2: items 1 and 2. At the owned stockpile without instruments, and at any setting with the stock owned and \(\tau^P=0\) at every date, Lemma H holds at every date, which is item 1, and step 1 at every date, which is item 2. For \(\mu<1\), if treatment never ceases for good, every date has a later treatment date, so \(\tau^W_t<0\) at every \(t\), the dates before the first treatment date included. The instruments \(z\) and \(\tau^X\) enter only through \(p^R\), \(r^K\), \(P^W\) and \(P^C\), which the proof takes as given.
Step 3: a positive fee requires a later tax. Let the stock be owned, \(\tau^P_s\ge0\) at every date, and \(\tau^W_t>0\). Were \(\tau^P_s=0\) at every \(s>t\), step 1 would give \(\tau^W_t\le0\). So \(\tau^P_s\ne0\), hence \(\tau^P_s>0\), at some \(s>t\).
Step 4: with nothing treated after \(t\), the fee is the discounted tax. At a date \(s\) that is not a treatment date, \(\varpi_s=0\), the first term of \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s\) is zero as in the proof of Lemma H, and \(c^W\left(0\right)=0\), so \(h^{\mathrm{mkt}}_s=-\tau^P_s\left[1-0-0\right]=-\tau^P_s\). If no date after \(t\) is a treatment date, the hypothesis on the price gives \(p^{\mathcal W}_t=-\sum_{s>t}w_{t,s}\tau^P_s\), and (GF) gives \(\tau^W_t=\sum_{s>t}w_{t,s}\tau^P_s\), the display of the statement. If moreover \(\tau^P_s\ge0\) at every \(s>t\) and \(\tau^P_{s'}>0\) at a date \(s'>t\) of positive weight, any later date when \(\mu<1\) and \(s'=t+1\) when \(\mu=1\), then \(\tau^W_t\ge w_{t,s'}\tau^P_{s'}>0\).

title: O.7 The sign of the gate fee without the emission tax
section: The weak sign does not need the forward sum
text:
The weak sign does not need the forward sum
The weak sign of item 2 holds without the hypothesis on the price of the waste stock, once \(J^W_{t+1}\left(\mathcal W_{t+1}\right)\) is read as the sector’s value, the supremum of the discounted cash flows of its plans from \(t+1\) on. Let \(\tau^P_s=0\) at every \(s>t\) and \(\mathcal W'_{t+1}>\mathcal W_{t+1}\). From the larger stock a plan can keep its acceptances \(W_s\), so every later handled flow is larger, \(H'_s\ge H_s\), and its treated flows \(T_s\) and recycling capital \(K^R_s\), at the share \(T_s/H'_s\) where \(H'_s>0\). It then recovers the same material, earns the same fees, pays the same rent and dumps the extra tonnes, free at \(\tau^P_s=0\). Its handling bill \(P^W_s\left[c^cT_s+H'_sc^T\left(T_s/H'_s\right)\right]\) is no larger, as \(P^W_s>0\) and \(H\,c^T\left(T/H\right)\) does not rise with \(H\) at fixed \(T\), \(c^T\left(\varpi\right)/\varpi\) being nondecreasing for a convex \(c^T\) with \(c^T\left(0\right)=0\). With \(\Lambda^{\mathrm{mkt}}>0\) its discounted cash flow exceeds the original’s by a sum of nonnegative terms, so \(J^W_{t+1}\) is nondecreasing, its derivative is nonnegative, and \(p^{\mathcal W}_t\ge0\), \(\tau^W_t\le0\). The strict signs and the two clauses on the tax use the forward sum.

title: O.8 The planner’s entry margin against open access
text:
The statement
Proposition 12 of the paper, stated in Appendix C, compares at one price vector the margin that decides whether the planner’s economy treats waste with the margins of the two economies without instruments, open access and the owned stockpile. It splits the difference into what the instruments and the property right add, says when the planner’s threshold is lower, and shows that the conditions for it are needed. This page proves it in full. Symbols are the paper’s, as on the notation page; a symbol the proof needs beyond them is defined where it is first used.
Appendix C states the proposition after this passage, which defines the identity it cites:
The three entry margins are functions of one price vector \(\left(C^N_N,p^S,F_K,p^P,p^W,\zeta,\Omega\right)\), and subtracting them at a common vector shows, term by term, what the instruments and the property right add. With \(V\) the virgin displacement value (V), \(V_0\equiv C^N_N+p^S\) its open-access counterpart, and \(\tilde F_K\equiv F_K\left(1-\zeta\Omega^Y\right)\),  \[
E^{\mathrm{pl}}-E^{\mathrm{OA}}
=\Big[\mathcal G^{x}\!\left(V,\tilde F_K\right)-\mathcal G^{x}\!\left(V_0,F_K\right)\Big]+p^P\left(1-d^W\right)-\zeta\Omega^Wc^c ,
\qquad
V-V_0=\zeta\Omega^NC^N_N+\left(\Omega^{N,S}+d^W\right)p^P .
\tag{I}
\]
Proposition 12 (the planner’s entry margin against open access). General primitives. Take a vector at which both economies extract, with \(F_K>0\), \(p^P>0\), the wedge inequalities \(1-\zeta\Omega^Y>0\) and \(1+\zeta\Omega^j>0\) for \(j\in\left\{N,W\right\}\), and \(\zeta=\sigma\left(p^W-p^M\right)\) for some \(\sigma\in\left[0,1\right]\) and some \(p^M\), as (Z) requires. There the identity (I) holds and its bracket is bounded on both sides by the value of the recovery gap at either intensity. At \(\phi^I=0\), so that \(\zeta=0\), the planner’s threshold is lower, \(E^{\mathrm{pl}}>E^{\mathrm{OA}}\), whatever the sign of \(p^W\). At \(\phi^I>0\) it is lower when \(\zeta\ge0\), which gives \(V\ge V_0\), and the diversion gain covers the collection wedge, \(p^P\left(1-d^W\right)>\zeta\Omega^Wc^c\). Each condition is needed: there are such vectors with \(\zeta<0\) in the liability phase (\(p^W>0\)), or with a large collection wedge, at which the ordering reverses. Against the owned stockpile, at a fee with \(1-\tau^W\Omega^Y>0\) and \(1+\tau^W\Omega^W>0\), the same identity holds with \(\zeta-\tau^W\) in place of \(\zeta\) in the three wedges and the overburden term \(\Omega^{N,S}p^P\) unchanged.
We take the simplest route for the paper’s assumptions. The proposition holds for general primitives, with no functional form: it compares functions of one price vector at one date, so its proof is algebra on the three margins, a lemma on the recovery value and two families of vectors built for the purpose. It uses no forward form of any price, and of the first-order conditions only those that put the three margins in terms of the vector. Like the entry condition of Section 4.2, the proposition “orders thresholds at a common point of the price space, not entry dates along paths whose states and prices differ”.
